The package's website includes a replication of the [duckspatial benchmark](https://cidree.github.io/duckspatial/articles/benchmark.html) to compare geoarrowrs, sedonadb, and duckspatial. In addition, there will be a geoarrowrs implementation of Apache Sedona [SpatialBench](https://github.com/apache/sedona-spatialbench) for a reference.

A formal CRAN release will indicate completion of the project followed by a join blog post with the R Consortium.

Upon successful completion, the `mask_sf()` capability will inform completion and development of the [`{sdf}`](https://github.com/JosiahParry/sdf) R package which provides a geometry-agnostic interface. I will contact the R-spatial organization and ask if the package can be formally integrated into the ecosystem.

## Budget & funding plan

I request $5,000 USD to fund the development of {geoarrowrs}.

### Milestone 1 - Complete Core Geometry Engine Implementation ($1,500)

This milestone funds the development effort to complete the core computation engine in {geoarrowrs} such that there is near-complete parity with {sf}. To accomplish the milestone, the following will be completed:

- Geometry reparation: `st_make_valid()`
- Geometry type checking: `st_geometry_try()` and `st_is()`
- Collection extraction: `st_collection_extract()`
- Perimeter calculation: `st_permiter()`
- Coordinate comparison: `st_equals_exact()`
- Jittering: `st_jitter()`
- Winding: `st_reverse()`
- Areal interpolation: `st_interpolate_aw()
- Bounding box: `st_bbox()`
- Polygon constructors:

The following features are out of scope of this proposal as there are no pure rust alternatives to rely on at present.

- 3D geometries
- Snapping
- Polygonization
- Geometry Projection

Completion is expected within 2 months of the award date.

### Milestone 2 - Persistent Spatial Indexes and Spatial Sorting ($1,000)

This milestone funds the development of creating and persisting spatial RTree and KDTree spatial indexes. These spatial indexes are created on the fly for each operation performed by {sf} as well as other libraries. For operations that require repeated look ups, persisting the index can be highly efficient.

Further, these indexes can be used to perform sorting of geometries to ensure that nearby geometries are orded together. Spatial sorting can greatly improve the effectiveness of row group statistics in GeoParquet files. Partial reads of a GeoParquet file can leverage the sorting more effectively.

For spatial sorting, Hilbert and sort-tile-recursive (STR) will both be supported. {geos} provides an STR tree, but it cannot be persisted to disk or used to sort geometries, and no other R package, to my knowledge, provides either capability.

Completion is expected within 3 months of the award date.

### Milestone 3 - {sf} Compatibility and CRAN release ($1,500)

In order for the package to be useful to the broadest community, this milestone will create drop in support for {sf} via S3 namespace masking. Users can call `mask_sf()` to overload the {sf} namespace with generics that enable {sf} to work with {geoarrowrs} geometries.

Following, documentation, examples, and benchmarks will be tidied up, and rewritten for ease of adoption.

One **risk** is that the source tarball is 14mb which is 9mb larger than the requested CRAN limit. However, exceptions can be made. For example, the prior art {rsgeo} was a [9mb tarball](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/rsgeo/). And other Rust based R packages such as {fcl}, are [15mb](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/fcl/) and supported on CRAN.

One **limitation** is that the `geo` crate that we rely on geometry operations does not have full spherical support whereas {sf} does via the {s2} package. In the event that a spherical CRS is used, geodesic algorithms will be used wherever possible. Otherwise, an error will be raised. {geoarrowrs} will not silently return a planar result for geographic coordinates—an issue [documented with painstaking detail](https://www.hypertidy.org/posts/2026-09-23_measures-sf-terra/).

Completion is expected within 5 months of the award date.

### Milestone 4 - GeoArrow and GeoParquet metadata ($1,000)

At present, geoarrowrs cannot propogate a coordinate reference system (CRS) across the R to Rust FFI boundary.
Milestone 3 is possible by leaning on {sf}'s CRS object and adding it as an attribute on the geoarrow vectors which requires PROJ to be installed.
This milestone would ensure that no external system dependencies would be needed.

Further, the GeoArrow specification records CRS as column level metadata in the projjson format.
To support this, the [`projjson-rs`](https://github.com/JosiahParry/projjson-rs/tree/main) crate was created which provides strongly typed reading and writing of `projjson` with no external system dependencies. As a result, GeoArrow transferred from DuckDB, R, Python, and GDAL would propagate the CRS correctly.

The column level metadata is also utilized by GeoParquet. As such, this milestone completely implements the GeoParquet 1.1 column metadata including:

- encoding
- geometry_types
- crs
- bbox
- covering
- orientation
- edges
- epoch

Of these, `covering` matters most. It records a bounding box column whose Parquet statistics allow a reader to skip row groups that cannot satisfy a spatial query, which, paired with the spatial sorting from Milestone 2, is what makes partial reads of a GeoParquet file effective.


Completion is expected within 6 months of the award date.
